output.decision: Do not launch a full multivariate test of hero, offer, and checkout this month. With 3,000 monthly sessions and a 2% purchase conversion rate, expected monthly orders are too limited for a practical, interpretable multivariate purchase-conversion test. Prioritize one high-impact, low-risk test or diagnostic work instead.
next_steps: Choose one primary hypothesis, preferably hero messaging/creative or offer presentation; avoid changing checkout concurrently.
Run a sample-size and duration calculation using the minimum detectable lift, traffic allocation, and desired confidence before committing.
Review funnel drop-off, device mix, payment/shipping friction, and qualitative session or customer-feedback evidence to identify the strongest single test candidate.
Keep checkout changes to QA, usability fixes, or clearly necessary defect remediation unless there is sufficient traffic for a dedicated test.
Predefine the primary metric (purchase conversion), guardrails (revenue per session, refund rate, checkout errors), eligibility, and stopping rules.
missing_inputs: Minimum detectable effect and required statistical confidence/power.
Current funnel conversion by step, device, and channel.
Whether offer changes affect margin, discounting policy, or returning-customer behavior.
Expected traffic changes or campaign launches this month.
assumptions: General ecommerce experimentation guidance is used because no library was supplied.
The 3,000 monthly sessions are approximately eligible test traffic and the 2% baseline applies to the intended audience.
Purchase conversion is the decision metric; a different higher-frequency metric could make a narrower test more feasible.
Simultaneously changing hero, offer, and checkout would make causal interpretation difficult even if traffic were adequate.
